title: ptrtoint to narrower-than-pointer int in aggregate initializer emits full pointer, dropping/overrunning following fields (miscompile + crash)
lines: 1686-1691 (root cause in bufferLEByte PtrToInt case); manifests in printWords 1196-1215 and printBytes 1154-1194
trigger: A global aggregate (struct/array) initializer in addrspace(1)/addrspace(4) containing `ptrtoint(@sym to iN)` where N*8 < pointer-size-in-bits (e.g. i32 under default 64-bit nvptx64 pointers), with at least one following field. Word-aligned layout -> silent miscompile; non-pointer-aligned/packed layout -> assertion crash (or report_fatal_error on PTX<7.1).
llc_cmd: /Users/justinlebar/code/llvm2/build/bin/llc -mtriple=nvptx64 -mcpu=sm_70 /tmp/final.ll -o -    # emits: .u64 s[1] = {g};  (drops 0x12345678, widens g to 64-bit). x86 cross-check: .long g / .long 305419896. Crash variant: packed <{i8,i32-ptrtoint,i8}> with -mcpu=sm_90 -> assertion nextSymbolPos>=pos in printBytes.

title: Kernel integer parameter with non-fundamental bit width emits invalid `.param .u<N>` type (e.g. .u48, .u24, .u3, .u17)
lines: 1486-1493 (emitFunctionParamList kernel scalar-int path); helper getPTXFundamentalTypeStr at 1256-1296
trigger: A ptx_kernel function taking an integer parameter whose bit width is not a valid PTX fundamental size (i2-i7, i17, i24, i33, i40, i48, i56, etc.). Non-kernel functions with the same params are fine (use promoteScalarArgumentSize).

title: Scoped f16/bf16 atomic add (llvm.nvvm.atomic.add.gen.f.{cta,sys}) drops mandatory .noftz qualifier, emitting malformed PTX with wrong FTZ semantics
trigger: Call llvm.nvvm.atomic.add.gen.f.cta.f16 / .sys.f16 / .cta.bf16 / .sys.bf16 (the scoped half/bfloat atomicAdd_block / atomicAdd_system intrinsics). f16 has no SM/PTX predicate so it triggers even on sm_70/ptx63; bf16 requires sm_90/ptx78.

title: InstCombine NVVM f16/f16x2 min/max/fma fold gates FTZ on half denormal mode while backend uses f32 mode, flipping flush-to-zero semantics
trigger: Any function whose f32 denormal mode differs from its default/half denormal mode, calling an f16 or f16x2 nvvm min/max/fma intrinsic, run through InstCombine (e.g. -O1). Concrete: denormal_fpenv(float: preservesign) makes f32 ftz ON, half ftz OFF; nvvm.fmin.f16 is the non-flushing variant, so for a subnormal-half input like 0x0001 (2^-24) and 1.0 the correct result is 2^-24, but after the fold the backend emits min.ftz.f16 which flushes the subnormal input to +0.0 and returns +0.0.
llc_cmd: opt -passes=instcombine -S in.ll -o opt.ll && llc -mtriple=nvptx64 -mcpu=sm_80 -mattr=+ptx70 opt.ll -o -   # emits min.ftz.f16 ; vs llc -mtriple=nvptx64 -mcpu=sm_80 -mattr=+ptx70 in.ll -o -   # emits the correct non-flushing min.f16

title: NVVMIntrRange: maxntid (or reqntid) with a 0 dimension creates ConstantRange(L,L) -> assertion crash on valid IR
mechanism: When a kernel has nvvm.maxntid with a zero component (e.g. "0" or "64,0,1"), getOverallMaxNTID returns the PRODUCT = 0, so MaxNTID=0 and MaxBlockDim.X = std::min(1024u, 0) = 0. The ntid.x case at line 132 calls addRangeAttr(MinBlockDim.X /*=1*/, MaxBlockDim.X + 1 /*=1*/, II). addRangeAttr (line 51) builds ConstantRange(APInt(32,1), APInt(32,1)). ConstantRange's ctor asserts ((Lower != Upper || Lower.isMaxValue() || Lower.isMinValue())); Lower==Upper==1 is neither min nor max => assertion fires. (The tid.x case addRangeAttr(0,0) is allowed because 0 is the min value, so the crash is specifically on the ntid path.) Root cause: the pass treats maxntid/reqntid dimension values as exact upper/lower bounds without validating against 0; a single 0 makes the product-derived bound 0 and yields a degenerate [L,L) range with L=1. The same shape arises for reqntid (e.g. reqntid="0" yields ntid.x range [0,1) intersected with the intrinsic's declared [1,1025) => empty [0,0)). In a release (no-assert) build, ConstantRange(1,1) is silently constructed as the full/empty set, degrading the assert into a wrong range. This pass runs in the clang -O{1,2,3} optimization pipeline (registerPipelineStartEPCallback in NVPTXTargetMachine.cpp:239-253), so the crash reproduces in normal clang CUDA compilation, not just standalone opt.
trigger: A ptx_kernel function with attribute nvvm.maxntid="0" (e.g. user writing __launch_bounds__(0)) that calls @llvm.nvvm.read.ptx.sreg.ntid.x(), compiled at -O1/-O2/-O3 (or opt -passes=nvvm-intr-range). Also triggered by any maxntid with a zero component such as "64,0,1".
llc_cmd: opt -S -mtriple=nvptx64-nvidia-cuda -mcpu=sm_90 -passes='default<O2>' < t.ll   (also: opt -passes=nvvm-intr-range; both crash with 'Assertion failed: Lower == Upper, but they aren't min or max value!' in ConstantRange.cpp:58)

title: Assertion `ArgOuts.size() == 1` in LowerCall for scalar integer call arg/return of 65-127 bits (i65/i72/i96)
trigger: A direct call returning or taking a scalar integer whose bit width is in [65,127] (e.g. i65, i72, i96). The callee/standalone definition compiles fine; only the call site asserts.

title: NVPTXLowerUnreachable::isLoweredToTrap is out of sync with UnreachableInst::shouldLowerToTrap (missing Naked check) -> unreachable block left with no terminator
trigger: Target with hasPTXASUnreachableBug() true (PTXVersion < 8.3, e.g. -mcpu=sm_60), -trap-unreachable enabled, and a function carrying the `naked` attribute whose body ends in `unreachable` (not preceded by a trap intrinsic). Confirmed with llc.

title: NVVMIntrRange: cluster_dim="0,0,0" (the AsmPrinter's recognized no-cluster form) folds cluster_ctaid/cluster_nctaid to an empty range => poison miscompile
mechanism: getClusterDim returns {0,0,0} for nvvm.cluster_dim="0,0,0". Because ClusterDim is non-empty, the !ClusterDim.empty() branch (lines 102-107) treats these as EXACT cluster dimensions: MinClusterDim = MaxClusterDim = {0,0,0}. Then cluster_ctaid.x (line 142) gets addRangeAttr(0, MaxClusterDim.X /*=0*/) = range [0,0) (empty), and cluster_nctaid.x (line 148) gets addRangeAttr(MinClusterDim.X /*=0*/, MaxClusterDim.X+1 /*=1*/) = [0,1) intersected with the intrinsic's declared range [1, INT_MIN) => empty [0,0). An empty range on a call result means the value is provably never in range, i.e. poison. But cluster.ctaid.x legitimately returns 0 at runtime (and cluster.nctaid.x returns >=1) when there is no cluster, so a well-defined program is turned into poison: after InstCombine the call carries range(i32 0,0) and every downstream use becomes poison/UB. Crucially, the NVPTXAsmPrinter (NVPTXAsmPrinter.cpp:488-492) explicitly treats cluster_dim with a leading 0 as the valid 'no explicit cluster' case (it asserts all dims are 0 and emits NO .reqnctapercluster), so {0,0,0} is a documented-valid attribute form. NVVMIntrRange's handling is inconsistent with the AsmPrinter: it should treat all-zero cluster_dim as 'no cluster info' rather than as exact dims of size 0.
trigger: A ptx_kernel with attribute nvvm.cluster_dim="0,0,0" that reads @llvm.nvvm.read.ptx.sreg.cluster.ctaid.x() (or cluster.nctaid.*/cluster.nctarank), compiled at -O1/-O2/-O3. The legal runtime ctaid.x=0 is forced to poison.
llc_cmd: opt -S -mtriple=nvptx64-nvidia-cuda -mcpu=sm_100 -passes='default<O2>' < t.ll   (shows: %ctaid.x = tail call range(i32 0, 0) i32 @llvm.nvvm.read.ptx.sreg.cluster.ctaid.x() -- empty/poison range)
